stories.headline: Houthis Seize Yemeni Lands as Tanker Attack Hits Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
Houthi rebel forces seized the Yemeni port of Mokha. The forces also took Mayyun Island near the Bab el-Mandab strait. The Saudi-backed Yemeni government lost these key coastal oil shipping lands to the Iran-aligned Houthis. Fighting across Yemen has displaced about 100,000 people.

A projectile hit the MT El Gaia tanker over the weekend in the Strait of Hormuz. The ship was sailing in dark mode with its identification system turned off. The tanker carried 25 crew members. Among them were 14 Indian nationals. The ship also carried 11 Pakistani nationals.

Pakistani Third Engineer Muhammad Hammad Obaida is missing after an engine room watch. Indian Oiler Sumit Kumar Singh is also missing. The Omani Coast Guard brought 23 remaining crew members ashore.

Iran's IRGC Navy said the ship hit naval mines on an illegal route. But the US said a missile and a drone hit the vessel.

Only four ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. Before the war, about 130 ships crossed each day. Saudi Aramco closed its East-West pipeline after a Houthi attack. Oil loadings stopped at the Saudi port of Yanbu. The price of Brent crude rose nearly 3% to $108 a barrel.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman talked with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo. They called for free navigation in the Red Sea. Egypt lost about $7 billion from the Suez Canal between 2023 and 2024. This was about 60 percent of canal revenues.

claims.text: Houthi rebel forces seized the Yemeni port of Mokha and Mayyun Island overlooking the Bab el-Mandab strait.
The Saudi-backed Yemeni government recently lost key coastal territories vital for oil shipping to the Iran-aligned Houthis.
An estimated 100,000 Yemenis have been displaced amid renewed fighting across Yemen.
The MT El Gaia tanker was hit by a projectile over the weekend in the Strait of Hormuz while operating in dark mode with its Automatic Identification System switched off.
The MT El Gaia had 25 crew members on board, including 14 Indian and 11 Pakistani nationals.
Pakistani Third Engineer Muhammad Hammad Obaida and Indian Oiler Sumit Kumar Singh remain unaccounted for after being on watch in the engine room of MT El Gaia when it was hit.
The Omani Coast Guard transferred 23 remaining crew members from MT El Gaia ashore following the attack.
Iran's IRGC Navy stated that the MT El Gaia struck naval mines while using an illegal route, whereas the US stated the vessel was hit by a missile and a drone.
Only four ships were recorded crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, compared with a prewar daily average of about 130 ships.
Saudi Aramco closed its East-West pipeline due to an attack by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.
The price of Brent crude rose nearly 3% to $108 a barrel following news that loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port of Yanbu were suspended.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea during talks in Cairo.
Egypt lost approximately $7 billion between 2023 and 2024, or about 60 percent of the Suez Canal's revenues, due to reduced Red Sea transit.

stories.headline: NATO Intercepts Drone Over Lithuania as Baltic Tensions Rise
stories.body:
NATO fighter jets shot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace overnight. The interception took place near the village of Pratkūnai. An Italian fighter jet carried out the shootdown for NATO. The unmanned aircraft had entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus.

Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas commented on the downed drone. Kaunas said authorities detected an explosive device on the drone. Bomb-disposal experts were called to the site. The experts neutralized the explosive device.

Military actions also escalated elsewhere in the region. Poland scrambled its own fighter jets as a preventive step. Russian jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles were carrying out strikes on Ukrainian territory.

Polish security forces later found a drone in the Baltic Sea. The aircraft was identified as a Russian drone. Forces recovered it near the beach in the town of Rusinowo.

Denmark reported another dangerous event in the Baltic Sea. A Russian frigate fired flares at a Danish air force helicopter. The helicopter was performing routine surveillance work. The incident occurred off Gedser in the Baltic Sea.

Danish Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus released details of the confrontation. Bruus said the Russian ship fired two flares at the helicopter. The warship gave no prior warning before firing. One of the flares passed within metres of the aircraft.

Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador to respond to the flare incident. The summons concerned the threat to the Danish air force helicopter.

Russian ambassador Vladimir Barbin addressed the Danish accusations. Barbin said Russia would thoroughly investigate the incident. But Barbin accused Danish helicopters of taking provocative actions. He said these actions occurred near Russian warships.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made a statement on retaliatory strikes. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery located in Syzran, Russia. He said the strike was a direct response to Russian attacks. Russia had targeted Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov commented on energy infrastructure attacks. Peskov mentioned a proposal from Donald Trump. Trump proposed a ceasefire on energy infrastructure. Peskov said the Kremlin considers Trump's proposal a good idea.

claims.text: NATO fighter jets shot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace overnight near the village of Pratkūnai.
An Italian fighter jet flying for NATO brought down the drone over Lithuania after it entered from Belarus.
Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas stated an explosive device detected on the downed drone was neutralized by bomb-disposal experts.
Poland scrambled fighter jets prevention-wise due to Russian jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory.
Polish security forces recovered a Russian drone from the Baltic Sea near the beach in Rusinowo.
Denmark reported that a Russian frigate fired flares at a Danish air force helicopter conducting routine surveillance off Gedser in the Baltic Sea.
Danish Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus stated that two flares were fired towards the helicopter without prior warning, with one passing within metres.
Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador over the Baltic Sea flare incident involving its air force helicopter.
Russian ambassador Vladimir Barbin stated Russia would thoroughly investigate the incident but accused Danish helicopters of provocative actions near Russian warships.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery in Syzran, Russia, in response to attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated the Kremlin considers Donald Trump's proposal for a ceasefire on energy infrastructure a good idea.

vocab.meaning: careful watching of an area or activity
intended to cause anger or action

stories.headline: US War With Iran Costs Billions and Depletes Interceptor Stockpiles
stories.body:
The Congressional Budget Office reported that the war with Iran has cost the US military $38 billion. This figure covers costs up to August 1, 2026. The report estimated the conflict adds $3 billion in military costs for every extra month. Rebuilding the depleted US stockpile of interceptors will take at least five years. These include Patriot, Thaad, and Navy interceptors.

A Pentagon inspector general report showed the US spent $22.3 billion on munitions alone through June 30. Total spending on the conflict reached $33.4 billion by that date. The CBO estimated the US has used between one-half and two-thirds of its missile defense interceptors since June 2025. CSIS estimated Patriot interceptors dropped from about 2,330 before the war to between 759 and 827 by July 27.

President Donald Trump denied reports of weapons shortages. Trump claimed US munitions supplies are virtually unlimited.

The US military lost four F-15E fighter jets, one F-35 fighter, and 30 MQ-9 Reaper drones through June 30. Three F-15E jets were destroyed by friendly fire over Kuwait on March 1. Another was lost over Iran in April. At least 11 US service members died in action through June 30. Seven died in non-hostile events. Another 417 were wounded.

The White House requested $87.6 billion in extra funding in June. The request set aside $67.1 billion for the Department of Defense.

claims.text: A Congressional Budget Office report estimated that the war with Iran has cost the US military at least $38 billion as of August 1, 2026.
The Congressional Budget Office estimated that the conflict with Iran would add $3 billion to US military costs for every additional month it continues.
The Congressional Budget Office reported that rebuilding the depleted US stockpile of Patriot, Thaad, and Navy interceptors would take at least five years.
A Pentagon inspector general report revealed the US spent $22.3 billion on munitions alone through June 30, with total conflict spending reaching $33.4 billion.
The CBO estimated the US has likely used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of missile defense interceptors since June 2025.
CSIS estimated US stocks of Patriot interceptors fell from about 2,330 before the war to between 759 and 827 as of July 27.
President Donald Trump denied reports of weapons shortages, claiming US munitions supplies are virtually unlimited.
The US military lost four F-15E fighter jets, one F-35 Joint Strike Fighter, and 30 MQ-9 Reaper drones during the war with Iran through June 30.
Three US F-15E fighter jets were destroyed by friendly fire over Kuwait on March 1, and another was lost over Iran in April.
Through June 30, at least 11 US service members were killed in action, seven died in non-hostile incidents, and 417 were wounded in the conflict with Iran.
The White House requested $87.6 billion in supplemental funding in June, with $67.1 billion earmarked for the Department of Defense.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Blocks Mail-In Ballot Restrictions Ahead of Midterm Elections
stories.body:
The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's plan for new Postal Service rules on mail-in ballots. The decision comes ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Justice Brett Kavanaugh agreed with the decision. Kavanaugh said state and local officials lacked enough time to implement the rule before the election. Supreme Court Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented from the ruling.

President Donald Trump criticized Justices Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett on Truth Social. Trump said they are not the people he interviewed.

Attorney General Todd Blanche said that the court decision will not affect ongoing criminal investigations into illegal voting. In Texas, federal prosecutors charged six lawful permanent residents and one undocumented immigrant for voting in federal elections over eight years.

US District Judge Deborah Boardman issued an injunction on September 2. The ruling blocked Donald Trump's executive order targeting birth tourism.

Mail-in voting for the midterm elections has already begun in several states. These states include Alabama, North Carolina, and Wisconsin.

claims.text: The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's plan to implement new Postal Service restrictions on mail-in ballots ahead of the November 3 midterms.
Justice Brett Kavanaugh concurred with the Supreme Court decision, stating that state and local officials lacked enough time to implement the mail ballot rule before the election.
Supreme Court Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented from the ruling that blocked the mail-in ballot restrictions.
President Donald Trump attacked Justices Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett on Truth Social, stating they are not the people he interviewed.
Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that the Supreme Court decision blocking mail-in voting restrictions will not affect ongoing criminal investigations into illegal voting.
Federal prosecutors in Texas charged six lawful permanent residents and one undocumented immigrant for voting in federal elections over the past eight years.
US District Judge Deborah Boardman issued a preliminary injunction on September 2 blocking Donald Trump's executive order targeting birth tourism.
Mail-in voting for the midterm elections has already begun in states including Alabama, North Carolina, and Wisconsin.

stories.headline: United States Confirms Deployment of Weapons in Earth Orbit
stories.body:
The United States confirmed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space. US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink spoke about the weapons at a conference. Meink said the US has on-orbit space control weapons. He said these weapons can defend forces against hostile actions.

Victoria Samson of the Secure World Foundation commented on the systems. Samson suggested the newly acknowledged weapons could be space-based jammers.

Russia and China warned of an arms race in outer space after the announcement. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun urged the US to stop expanding military capabilities in space. Guo also asked the US to stop preparing for war in outer space. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia counts on international efforts to completely demilitarise space.

Dr. Bleddyn Bowen said China has shown space tug capability. This allows a vehicle to grab a satellite and move it into another orbit. India conducted an Anti-Satellite missile test in March 2019 under Mission Shakti. That test destroyed an Indian satellite in low-Earth orbit.

claims.text: The United States confirmed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space.
US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink stated at a conference that the US has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending forces against hostile adversary action.
Victoria Samson of the Secure World Foundation suggested that the newly acknowledged US space systems could be space-based jammers.
Russia and China warned of an arms race in outer space following the US confirmation of an orbital weapon deployment.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun urged the US to stop expanding its military capabilities and preparing for war in outer space.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated Russia counts on broad international consolidation toward the complete demilitarisation of space.
Dr. Bleddyn Bowen stated China has demonstrated space tug capability, allowing a vehicle to grapple a satellite and move it into a different orbit.
India conducted an Anti-Satellite missile test in March 2019 under Mission Shakti, destroying an Indian satellite in low-Earth orbit.

vocab.meaning: to remove military weapons or forces from an area
the path of an object around a planet or star

stories.headline: India Introduces Merchant Fees for UPI Payments Over 2,000 Rupees
stories.body:
The National Payments Corporation of India introduced a new fee framework for UPI merchant payments. The Merchant Discount Rate framework takes effect on October 15. NPCI issued a circular about the rule on Tuesday, September 15, 2026.

Under the framework, customers will pay no charges for making UPI payments. This zero-fee rule for consumers applies regardless of transaction value. NPCI explicitly barred UPI app providers from charging platform fees to consumers. App providers are also barred from adding any other charges to consumers for UPI payments.

Merchants receiving UPI payments above Rs 2,000 in a single transaction will pay a 0.4% fee. The fee is capped at a maximum of Rs 300. Small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month will pay no fees on incoming payments.

The Union Ministry of Finance issued the official notification under Section 10A of the 2007 Payment and Settlement Systems Act. Parliament passed the 2026 Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill in August 2026. That bill amended the 2007 law to allow charges on UPI and RuPay debit card payments.

The Indian government said that data analysis shows only 4% of merchant UPI transactions will be impacted. Standard credit card fees typically range from 1.5% to 2.5% per transaction, according to NPCI.

The Finance Ministry said that collected fees will be shared among payment participants. These participants include banks and app providers. The money will support operations and system expansion. A dedicated fund will receive 5% of total MDR collections. This fund will promote UPI usage by small merchants.

A flat fee of Rs 5 will apply to UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 in essential sectors. These sectors include railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel, and agricultural inputs. Essential sectors account for nearly 17% of merchant UPI transaction volume. They also account for around 46% of merchant transaction value.

Capital market transactions will attract a fee of 0.02%. This applies to mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers, and dealers. The fee is capped at Rs 300 per transaction.

Person-to-person UPI transfers will remain completely free for individuals. These transfers account for 37% of total UPI transaction volume. They also account for 70% of total UPI transaction value.

Opposition parties in India criticized the new fee. They called the charge the "Modi tax". Congress media head Pawan Khera spoke out against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Khera said Modi popularised UPI for a cashless economy and is now taxing people for using it. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged that Modi surrendered to American pressure. Gandhi said American payment companies had opposed India's zero-fee policy.

The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) issued a circular on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, introducing the 0.4% MDR on UPI merchant transactions over Rs 2,000.
Under the new NPCI framework, customers will pay no charges for making UPI payments regardless of transaction value.
NPCI explicitly restricted UPI application providers from charging platform fees or any other charges to consumers for UPI payments.
Merchants receiving UPI payments above Rs 2,000 in a single transaction will be levied a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), with an upper cap of Rs 300.
Small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month will pay no fees on incoming UPI payments.
The Union Ministry of Finance issued the notification regarding UPI merchant charges under Section 10A of the 2007 Payment and Settlement Systems Act.
In August 2026, Parliament passed the 2026 Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill, which amended the 2007 Payment and Settlement Systems Act to allow charges on UPI and RuPay debit card payments.
The Indian government stated that data analysis shows only 4% of merchant UPI transactions will be impacted by the introduction of the MDR.
According to NPCI, standard credit card Merchant Discount Rates typically range from 1.5% to 2.5% per transaction.
The Finance Ministry stated that MDR fees collected will be distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and app providers, to support operations and expansion.
A dedicated fund for promoting UPI usage by small merchants will be established using 5% of total MDR collections.
A flat MDR rate of Rs 5 will apply to UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 in essential sectors including railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel, and agricultural inputs.
Essential sectors subject to the flat Rs 5 MDR account for nearly 17% of person-to-merchant UPI transaction volume and around 46% of transaction value.
Capital market UPI transactions for mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers, and dealers will attract an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300 per transaction.
Person-to-person UPI transfers account for 70% of total UPI transaction value and will remain completely free for individuals.
Person-to-person UPI transactions constitute 37% of total UPI transaction volume and 70% of transaction value.
Opposition parties in India criticized the government's decision to levy a 0.4% MDR on UPI merchant payments above Rs 2,000, calling it the 'Modi tax'.
Congress media head Pawan Khera stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi popularised UPI for a cashless economy and is now taxing people for using it.
Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi surrendered to American pressure after US payment companies opposed India's zero-MDR policy.
